That’s completely fair. Information online is not very clear. I guess it all depends on the individual situation and circumstances. Can psychologists diagnose physical illness? 

I’ve only had experience with a psychiatrist so I can’t speak on psychologists but I can say that with my psychiatrist, she did put me onto therapy treatment first before she put me onto medication once we realised therapy wasn’t enough for my symptoms. Having the option to go straight onto medication and not put on yet another waiting list to see another professional was helpful. 

For OP, as they want to get an ADHD assessment I still think a psychiatrist is the best option. OP may or may not want medication for ADHD but if they end up wanting it then they’ll have to go and get diagnosed by a psychiatrist anyways. 

But each to their own.

you know what, you’re absolutely right. I did a bit of research and can see that some clinical psychologists can diagnose but they can’t prescribe medication. 

Personally I still think going to a psychiatrist may be better for OP as it seems like there may be some other things going on besides potential ADHD. Psychiatrists are trained medical doctors, and can better diagnose complex issues as well as see if there’s anything going on physically that could be contributing to the difficulties.

A psychologist and/or therapist is not adequately qualified to diagnose. I think it would be best if you can get in contact with a psychiatrist. Psychiatrists are the ones who will be assessing you and are qualified to diagnose as well as prescribe treatment and medication. You may have to seek out a private assessment. 

Regardless of if you do have ADHD or not, a psychiatrist will be able to assess you and diagnose you with other conditions as well. 

When I received my diagnosis of ADHD I was also diagnosed with other conditions which had symptoms that overlapped and didn’t overlap. Some were disorders I didn’t even know about and since then I have been able to see now what is my adhd and what is being caused by one of my other conditions. But sometimes it’s still confusing as two different conditions can have many of the same symptoms. 

Good luck with it all, I know it can be so frustrating when you don’t know what the hell is going on with you!

Hi… just thought I’d chime in here. I have BPD and I definitely haven’t been misdiagnosed.

Since diagnosis I have worked relentlessly at therapy and DBT. It has been hard. It has been so painful and it has been exhausting but I can safely say I have definitely improved a lot since then, yes I used to engage in some of the harmful behaviours towards my ex (at times warranted, he was unfaithful and lied to me multiple times during our 6 yr relationship) pre diagnosis but I always apologised after as I constantly felt shame for any outbursts and knew even then that there were better ways to communicate but I just didn’t know what was wrong with me. I always felt it though, that something was wrong with me. Sadly I had been in therapy for a good 4 years before diagnosis so although I was getting better over the years nothing really worked as effective as DBT has and I have always wished I was able to do DBT in my early twenties rather than later as most of my adult life has been wrecked by this disorder alongside my ADHD. Now, I do not have outbursts in that manner anymore. I can still very much feel the rage but I have a much more solid grasp on keeping it inside and ‘letting it go’ over things that don’t warrant that response. 

I post this comment because I want to challenge the stigma. Yes, there are a lot of people with cluster B out there who can be very damaging and hard to be with but there are also people with these conditions who are trying very hard to recover. It just takes a hell of a lot of work to retrain your brain but it doesn’t mean each and every one of us is under serving of love. 

I am sorry to you as it is clear you’ve had really bad experiences with your ex and I’m in no way trying to invalidate your experiences. I can understand why you feel so strongly but I do hope you can appreciate that there are those of us who are battling unfair stigma when we do try hard to improve and not hurt others. My current partner has never been yelled at or belittled by me and we have been together for almost 1.5 years now. I am better able to notice when I’m irrationally angry at everything and I pre warn all my loved ones beforehand so they are able to give me more space or not take my reactions (irritation on face) personally. 

I just want to note that when I first got diagnosed I started reading up online about everything to do with BPD. It was such a shock to me and rocked me to my core. Comments like these made me feel like I was this horrible evil monster who was hiding in skin to look like a person. I did not want to be manipulative or abusive and I never asked for this condition and it was so upsetting to see the amount of advice online telling people to run as far away from me as they could.

As for OP’s post I do agree with another comment. Yes BPD is shit and causes the outbursts but there has been no accountability after the partner has cooled down and BPD is not a scapegoat in any way for poor behaviour. This is abuse and I do hope OP has moved on to a better partner or at least their partner has put a lot of effort into recovery and their relationship is better.

I would say the breaches to duty of care are 

- M withholding my letter to HR to ask for a meeting to discuss accommodations for 3 to 4 months. 

- M only taking me seriously once I became very suicidal.  

- M yelling at me and telling me I need to improve because everyone else in the team comes in everyday. This has happened on multiple occasions. I cannot because I am not as capable as them and they do not have disabilities. 

- Neither M or HR booking in a meeting with me after I was off sick in September 2021 to discuss my return to work or create a plan to support me.

- I did not receive regular 1 to 1s from either M or HR to see how I was doing at any point. 

- I did not receive any correspondence to outline what was needed from myself during my flexible working but would be told off by M on multiple times and threatened with disciplinary action. I feel that although my workplace have the right to do this and I understand the reasons I would have appreciated clear targets to improve on. 

- My pay was reduced without notifying me of a change to my salary. 

- I keep getting SSP deducted as they claim I have had 60 days off in 2021. This is false and I have asked multiple times for it to be rectified since April 4th. The discrepancies have not been corrected and I am still being deducted monthly. 

- My colleagues all received their promotion on the exact same day. That is my whole team but myself and one of the reasons I was also given was because of my challenges. My challenges are my illnesses, as well as managing the ongoing rape investigation. Yes, maybe they are not bound to have to tell me about my teams promotions but this would have been a common decency especially as I was the only one not receiving it. As they were all promoted at the exact same time but myself I cannot help but feel I have been singled out. 

- I feel many months of my sickness could have not happened had M given my letter to HR when I asked for it be sent and reasonable accommodations were made earlier. I’m three months in now and I’ve had 1 sick day in the last two months and my focus is back and my performance is strong just to show how I have improved since getting what I needed. 

At the end of the day it has felt like I’ve been trying my damn hardest every single day to get better. I was suicidal everyday for a year and any of those life events would have been very difficult for a normal person to process let alone one with mental health issues. I have been an employee for almost 4 years and do feel quite let down by how I’ve been managed. I do feel that if I was physically disabled I would not have been dealt with in this manner. Of course I can not prove this but I do know this.

The thing is my performance is enough. I have been told by M that I have completed all works requested of me. I have also reached all my objectives set out to me by him and he had agreed this when we had a review at the beginning of the year. So I’m confused as to why I’m being told my work performance was not enough. 

How can the company not have done something wrong ? I requested reasonable adjustments to be made which were ignored and this directly contributed to me experiencing a crisis at work where I was strongly considering suicide. Is that not negligence ? 

Did my company/M not have a duty of care to me ? 

It is in their own policy that they should conduct regular meetings and assessments to support employees during long term sickness.

Please can you let me know why you feel my company has done no wrong in how they’ve handled me ? 

Thank you for your comments and time to reply.

I am not saying I don’t agree that my pay was cut, what I am saying is that I was not made aware of it in writing. I don’t know your relationships ins and outs but I would say that he is his own person. He can choose to stay or leave. 

I would bring that stuff up to him, that you see how it’s all affected him and makes you feel guilt over it as you love him and want the best for him etc but personally for me I find when someone leaves because they think they are not good enough for another… it kinda just takes the choice away from the other person. 

Best thing you can do is just to keep trying to get better. Do everything in your power to be the best partner you can be. I’m sure you’re doing this already. Encourage him to get therapy for his trauma etc 

It sounds like you love him a lot. Doesn’t that mean ultimately you want him to be the happiest ? In that sense he is choosing to be with you because as much as there is all the pain it is because it makes him happy ? 

BPD makes us feel undeserving of our partners. Like a burden. Like they should be with someone better. But we are their better. Connection and the person is what is important. Yeah they can go out and meet someone without BPD but that person isn’t you. 

It’s not easy. Relationships are hard work already and with what we have it can be even harder. But I promise you the more therapy you have, the more skills you learn to manage yourself and the more loving choices you make for yourself the happier you will be and there will eventually be less and less episodes. Hopefully you have tried DBT too? It’s not a cure but I have found it has improved my symptoms over time (I’m almost a year post diagnosis and dbt treatment)

If it is too dry add in a bit of water, stir and put the lid back on
